MC: What do we call it when one method invokes another to do most or all of the work?

column5: Generalization is when we add a parameter to a function to make its capabilities more general.
Delegation is when one method passes responsibility to another method to do most or all of the work.
Inheritance is the ability to define a new class that is a modified version of a previously defined class.
Specialization is a way of using inheritance to create a new class that is a specialized version of an existing class.

class Hand(Deck):
    def __init__(self, label=''):
        self.label = label
        self.cards = []

When we create a Hand with Hand('player 1'), which __init__ methods run?

column5: Hand would inherit Deck.__init__ only if it didn't define its own; because it does, its version overrides the one in Deck.
Python doesn't run the parent's __init__ automatically -- if the child class defines __init__, only the child's version runs.
